To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LO-sets in multi-objective combina-torial optimization problems under set dominance, epsilon, and hyper-volume preference relation are not the same, and that the number of LO-set increases with problem non-linearity.

1) LO-sets under hypervolume and set-dominance tend to be more similar than LO-sets under dominance and hypervolume; 2) LO-sets of a fixed cardinality under epsilon are typically different from those under set dominance or hypervolume; and 3) LO-sets tend to decrease with the number of objective functions, and increase with the problem nonlinearity.
LO-sets of multi-objective combina- torial optimization problems are typically numerous, and that LO-set cardinality under set- dominance and hypervolume are correlated, but not under epsilon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the structure and properties of multi-objective local optimal sets.
a better understanding of LO-sets and their relation, which is a fundamental issue in multi-objective local optimization.
the analysis of the structure of LO-sets under several definitions of neighborhood and set preference relations, and with their relation with each other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LO-sets of different cardinality under set dominance, hypervolume, or epsilon, are not the same.
the set-based dominance relation is a stronger notion of optimality than the epsilon and hypervolme ones, and thus, it can lead to better approximation guarantees.
LO-sets are problem-specific and that the choice of the preference relation is a key factor to consider when designing multi-objective local algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, LO-sets of multi-objective combi-natorial problems under epsilon or hypervisor are not the same, and that the set-dominance relation is the strictest among the three.
, in general, set-dominance and epsilon-based LO-sets are closer to each other than to hypervolume-based LO-sets.
LO-sets are problem-dependent, but the more similar they are to LO-sets of the set dominance relation, the easier they are to identify, and the more likely they are to be found.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the set-based dominance relation is the least restrictive, and thus the easiest to satisfy, among the set preference relations considered in this work.
, for multi-objective optimization problems, the choice of LO-set is a crucial design decision that has a direct influence on performance.
the set-based dominance relation is not a good proxy for the hypervolume and epsilon indicator.
